newsitem.title: UK: Japan GSP copper/zinc rise slight surprise.
newsitem.headline: Japan GSP copper/zinc rise slight surprise.

text.p: The level of Japanese 1997/98 imports of copper and zinc under a tariff-free programme exceeded expectations, but were only mildly surprising, analysts here said.
Under the Generalised System of Preferences (GSP) scheme Japan imported 75,631 tonnes of copper and 112,639 tonnes of zinc, up on 1996/97 levels, but lead imports dropped slightly to 14,117 tonnes.
"There were factors, such as the new tax rises, but certainly they are encouraging," William Adams of London Metal Exchange (LME) trader Rudolf Wolff and Co said.
Traditionally, Japan imports major tonnages of metal from developing countries in the first quarter to be custom-cleared tariff-free on April 1.
In 1996/97, Japan imported 63,886 tonnes of copper, 83,535 tonnes of zinc, and 15,452 tonnes of lead.
This year, Japanese metal demand appears to have been strong in the first quarter because internal consumption taxes are being raised from three percent to five percent on April 1.
"Zinc is a larger increase than expected, but there is good demand in the Japanese galvanising sector," Helen Williamson of LME trader Brandeis (Brokers) Ltd said.
There had been some expectations that copper imports would be lower in 1997/98, because of the high price and backwardation that has persisted in the market.
But "the backwardation has eased, so there may have been some late buying ahead of the tax rise," Williamson said.
It was also likely that Japanese end-users would be re-stocking, Adams noted.
However, in the medium-term physical demand from Japan is expected to fall off.
"That (the GSP) is a factor out of the way. Metal bought in the first quarter will be consumed in the second quarter," Angus MacMillan of LME trader Billiton Metals Ltd said.
